anti_overlap: fd-trust-boundary-governance covers the encrypted transfer protocol and trust-boundary crossing; this agent covers pre-transfer raw handling, purge discipline, and failure-state distinctness
fd-haccp-critical-control-throughput (this batch) covers CCP/throughput tradeoffs; this agent covers retention/minimization/purge-audit discipline specifically

fd-dicom-deidentification-recall (this batch) covers metadata/pixel de-identification completeness; this agent covers raw-retention lifecycle and access accounting, not the de-identification content itself
decision_lens: If a regulator or auditor asked 'prove that raw footage for session X was never retained longer than necessary and was only purged after downstream confirmation,' could the manifest alone answer that — including who/what accessed the raw footage while quarantined, and why a not-yet-purged session hasn't been purged yet?
distance_rationale: Same abstraction level (a system that ingests bulk raw signal, structurally guarantees minimization before any output leaves a controlled boundary, and enforces retention/purge discipline under audit) but an entirely different regulatory and industry context — telecom LI systems are built around 'never retain more than the mandate allows' rather than JawnScope's aesthetic/consent-driven privacy design.
expected_isomorphisms: LI mediation systems structurally separate raw intercepted signal (never persisted beyond the mandate window, access-logged, purge-verified) from the minimized/authorized output handed to requesting agencies, with purge only occurring after delivery confirmation and an unconfirmed-delivery record never being force-purged nor left in indefinite limbo — this maps directly onto quarantine-raw handling, the 'reclaim wired but not armed' verify-then-delete design, and the dead-letter requirement for sessions whose sinks never confirm.
focus: Whether raw-retention minimization, purge-only-after-confirmed-delivery, and dead-letter handling for stuck sessions meet the rigor LI/CALEA mediation systems require for defensibility under audit — specifically around access control to quarantined raw and the finality/logging of purge decisions.
name: fd-lawful-intercept-minimization
review_areas: Whether access to quarantined raw (during the local operator-drain window, ahead of the encrypted device→node protocol) is logged at all, or only the eventual reclaim_events/verified_sinks are recorded — LI systems log every touch of raw signal, not just the final disposition

Whether the 'reclaim wired but not armed' design (decision 9) has an explicit, bounded operator-visible queue of 'eligible for purge but not yet purged' sessions, or whether that state is invisible until someone thinks to check

Whether the dead-letter path (required by the storage-ceiling policy in CLAUDE.md §3) is actually implemented in this M2 slice for sessions whose redact_video stage crashes or never confirms, or only reclaim-side confirmation is handled
Whether purge/reclaim decisions, once made, are irreversible and logged (append-only) the way LI purge-certification records are, versus being a mutable manifest field that could be silently altered

Whether the manifest distinguishes 'no redaction needed' from 'redaction attempted and failed' from 'redaction not yet attempted' — LI systems require these to be structurally distinct states so a failure can never be mistaken for a pass

severity_examples.condition: No explicit 'redaction_failed' or dead-letter state exists distinct from 'redaction_pending' — an operator or automated sweep could mistake a crashed session for one simply not yet processed, risking either premature raw purge or indefinite silent quarantine.
severity_examples.scenario: A session's redact_video stage throws mid-clip (e.g. ONNX runtime crash) and the pipeline leaves the session in whatever partial manifest state existed at crash time, indistinguishable in the schema from a session that hasn't started redaction yet.

severity_examples.condition: The manifest's provenance/lineage only begins recording at contributor_ingest; nothing records raw-file access prior to or outside that stage, so 'was raw ever copied/viewed before ingest' is unanswerable.
severity_examples.scenario: Quarantined raw sits in `~/JawnScope/quarantine-inbox/` for the manual-drain window with no access log — any process or operator action touching those files leaves no trace in the session manifest.

severity_examples.condition: An eligible-for-purge backlog could grow unnoticed since nothing surfaces it, defeating the purpose of computing eligibility in the first place.
severity_examples.scenario: The reclaim_events prerequisites (verified_sinks, checksums) are computed and stored, but there's no operator-facing surface listing 'these N sessions are reclaim-eligible now' — the design in decision 9 is described as computed-but-inert with no visibility mechanism mentioned.

source_domain: Telecommunications — lawful intercept (LI) / CALEA compliance engineering, data minimization under legal mandate
success_hints: Look for a distinct, named dead-letter/failed state in the session manifest schema, separate from pending and complete
Look for any access-logging concept applied to the pre-ingest quarantine window, not just post-ingest lineage
Look for an operator-visible surface (even just a query/report) over reclaim-eligible-but-not-yet-reclaimed sessions
Flag any purge/reclaim mechanism described as reversible or silently mutable rather than append-only/logged
